General_Description.Text: Ce3D is a tissue clearing method designed to enhance 3D microscopy by providing strong tissue transparency, preserving reporter protein fluorescence, and maintaining the capacity for immunolabeling. The method involves the use of N-methylacetamide and Histodenz to achieve a refractive index matching medium, which is combined with Triton X-100 and 1-thioglycerol to clear tissues. The final Ce3D medium has a refractive index ranging between 1.49 and 1.5. This method is suitable for large volumetric imaging and preserves cellular morphology, making it ideal for high-resolution quantitative Histo-Cytometry. Ce3D also supports multiplex imaging and is compatible with various antibodies and fluorophores.

Tissue_Types.Text4: lymph node, lung, kidney, liver, mammary gland, small intestine, brain, bones, heart, and muscle.
Text4_Reference: Overview of the procedure: 'Using Ce3D, we have achieved clearing and large volumetric imaging of various murine tissue types, including lymph node, lung, kidney, liver, mammary gland, small intestine, and brain (Figs. 2 and 3, Table 1), and have also used the method to image bones, heart, and muscle. We also attained robust staining, Ce3D clarification, and imaging of human biopsy samples of lymphoid tissues, liver, gut, and other tissues, suggesting that this technology is applicable to clinical studies (data not shown).'

Time_Consumption.Text1: Ce3D tissue clearing requires an incubation time of 12-72 hours at room temperature, depending on tissue size, with the clearing medium replaced once during the incubation for larger tissue samples.
Text1_Reference: SUPPLEMENTARY METHODS: 'Ce3D Tissue Clearing: Stained and washed tissues were placed in the Ce3D medium inside a chemical fume hood and incubated at room temperature on a rotor for 12-72 hours. Total incubation time depended on tissue size, with the clearing medium replaced once during the incubation for larger tissue samples.'

Time_Consumption.Text2: Ce3D clearing is fast, achieving robust transparency of most tissues within 24 h.
Text2_Reference: Abstract: 'Ce3D clearing is fast, achieving robust transparency of most tissues within 24 h, albeit still necessitating additional time for staining, imaging, and analysis (1–2 weeks).'

Time_Consumption.Text3: Add Ce3D solution to the tissues and incubate them for 20 min at RT. Replace the solution with fresh Ce3D solution and incubate the tissues for an additional 30 min.
Text3_Reference: Box 1  Detection of RNA with Ce3D FISH

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text1: Ce3D preserves reporter protein and antibody-based fluorescence, as evidenced by experiments with Confetti reporter mouse tissues, which maintained fluorescence of GFP, YFP, RFP, and CFP reporter proteins with or without Ce3D treatment.
Text1_Reference: SUPPLEMENTARY FIGURE LEGENDS, Supplementary Figure 5: 'Ce3D preserves reporter protein and antibody-based fluorescence. (A) Confetti reporter mouse tissues were examined for fluorescence of GFP, YFP, RFP and CFP reporter proteins with or without Ce3D treatment.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text2: Ce3D treatment showed that no incompatible probes were seen among all tested reagents, and it was compatible with a wide range of tested antibodies and fluorophores, including CFP, GFP, YFP, tdTomato, DsRed, Alexa dyes, Brilliant violet, Pacific Blue, eFluor, and others.
Text2_Reference: SUPPLEMENTARY TABLE LEGENDS, Table 3: 'Tested antibodies (left) and fluorophores (right) that were found compatible with Ce3D treated tissues. No incompatible probes were seen among all tested reagents.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text3: Alexa fluorophores, GFP, YFP, RFP, CFP, and DsRed
Text3_Reference: Overview of the procedure: 'Similarly, major organic fluorophore families, such as Alexa fluorophores, perform extremely well with the Ce3D clearing procedure, thereby permitting robust fluorescent multiplexing. Finally, unlike alcoholbased clarification methods, Ce3D preserves reporter protein fluorescence, and, to date, we have successfully visualized tissues from GFP, YFP, RFP, CFP, and DsRed reporter animals without substantial loss of fluorescence over time.'

Application.Text4: Ce3D facilitates high-resolution, large volumetric imaging of lungs, allowing visualization from anterior to posterior surfaces with a total imaged depth of 3mm using two-photon excitation.
Text4_Reference: Supplementary Figure 9: 'High-resolution, large volumetric imaging of Ce3D treated tissues. Lungs were labeled with Alexa 647 conjugated anti-cytokeratin antibody and cleared with Ce3D... Total imaged depth was 3mm.'

Application.Text5: Ce3D collectively allowing quantitative characterization of cells with respect to their spatial positioning within tissues on the basis of phenotypic and functional markers.
Text5_Reference: Abstract: 'These characteristics permit high-quality multiplex fluorescence microscopy of large tissue volumes, as well as image analysis using advanced platforms such as volumetric histocytometry, collectively allowing quantitative characterization of cells with respect to their spatial positioning within tissues on the basis of phenotypic and functional markers.'

Application.Text6: Together, these detailed procedures and solutions for high-resolution volumetric microscopy with Ce3D enable quantitative visualization of cells and tissues at a high level of detail, allowing exploration of cellular spatial relationships in a variety of tissue settings.
Text6_Reference: Abstract: 'Together, these detailed procedures and solutions for high-resolution volumetric microscopy with Ce3D enable quantitative visualization of cells and tissues at a high level of detail, allowing exploration of cellular spatial relationships in a variety of tissue settings.'

Application.Text7: Ce3D can also be coupled with histocytometry to achieve a quantitative understanding of cellular phenotypic states directly within 3D tissues (Fig. 5). Ultimately, this can lead to a better understanding of how tissue microenvironments shape cellular states and, conversely, how cellular positioning can influence the function of the examined tissue in both healthy and diseased states.

Note.Text7: In particular, brains treated with conventional fixatives and Ce3D reagents require extended clarification times, presumably due to a high degree of tissue lipidation and marked reduction in the penetration and equilibration speed of the Ce3D clearing reagent.

Note.Text8: It may take several days for antibodies to penetrate uniformly into the deeper tissue regions, and each organ type necessitates empirical testing of the concentration and staining duration for specific probes and fluorophores.
